predecessors.name: Sparta (Peloponnesian League)
predecessors.text: the coastal cities of Laconia, which Flamininus 'separated ... from Spartan rule and placed ... under Achean protection'

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: the Laconian coastal cities, whose koinon 'continued until 297 AD when the Emperor Diocletian reformed the provincial administration'

ledger.x: 195: the coastal Laconian cities become independent under Achaean protection.

146: the cities join the Lacedaemonian League. after the dissolution of the Achaean League the Free Laconians joined the Lacedaemonian League, a koinon of Spartan colonies under Roman rule; no separate dossier exists for that koinon.
21 BC: Augustus re-establishes the League of Free Laconians.

wars.name: War against Nabis
wars.outcome: Flamininus besieged Sparta and Nabis surrendered Argos and the coastal cities of Laconia and his fleet; the cities became the League of Free Laconians under Achaean protection.

wars.name: Nabis's war on Gythium
wars.outcome: Nabis besieged and retook Gythium and took Las; the Achaean fleet was beaten by Sparta's new fleet and Philopoemen could not defeat the Spartans outside Gythium; the Achaeans then ravaged Laconia for thirty days.

certainty.note: The pages name Gythium and Las only; the shape is two discs and the real extent of the coastal cities and their territory is not given.
